newsitem.title: USA: SEC brings action against Arizona firm over bonds.
newsitem.headline: SEC brings action against Arizona firm over bonds.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission on Wednesday said it settled securities fraud charges against financial adviser Peacock, Hislop, Staley & Given Inc over bonds sold in 1993 by Maricopa County, Ariz.

As part of the settlement, announced by the SEC's Los Angeles office, the Phoenix, Ariz.,-based firm has agreed to pay $50,000 in fines and partner Larry Given has agreed to $25,000 in fines for their involvement in the bond deals.
Also as part of the settlement, the firm consented to the entry of the SEC order and to pay the fines, but neither admitted nor denied any of the SEC's findings.
Robert Casillas, a senior vice president with the firm, said the settlement was appropriate.

"Our settlement, without admitting or denying the commission's findings, was the prudent course of action for our business and our clients," Casillas said. "The resolution of this matter without protracted litigation enables us to keep our focus on providing quality services to our clients."

"As a small regional firm, the settlement of this matter avoids the huge costs, which would be associated with having an ultimate determination of the merits of the SEC's case by the judicial system," Casillas said.
The SEC settlement with Peacock, Hislop, Staley & Given Inc capped its two year probe of municipal bond issues by the Arizona county, the sixth largest county in the nation.
People familiar with the matter said that additional actions by the SEC arising from its investigation of Maricopa County were unlikely.

Earlier this week, the SEC instituted cease and desist proceedings against Maricopa County. The SEC alleged in that action that the county violated the anti-fraud provisions of the federal securities laws in connection with the July 1993 offer and sale of two series of general obligation bonds.
Earlier on Wednesday, Maricopa County's Board of Supervisors, meeting in Phoenix, approved a proposed settlement with the SEC.
Peacock, Hislop, Staley & Given Inc and Larry Given had served as financial adviser to the county and prepared the official statements for the 1993 bond issues.
The official statements were the primary disclosure documents for the offerings.
The SEC alleged that the firm and Given "caused and aided and abetted" Maricopa County in violating securities laws in connection with the two 1993 bond offerings.
The official statements contained financial information about the county for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1992.

However, the county's financial condition at the time of the offerings had materially worsened and the county developed a deficit in its general fund. The SEC said the official statements failed to disclose these changes.

In addition, the official statements for one of the offerings represented that bond proceeds would be used to finance specific county projects when in fact the county used the funds to finance its deficit, the SEC alleged.

"Despite knowing of the county's plan, PHS&G (Peacock, Hislop, Staley & Given Inc), through Given, did not revise or supplement or cause the county to revise or supplement its official statement to reflect this plan," the SEC said.
The SEC actions in Maricopa County were precedent setting because they were the first by the commission against a general purpose issuer of municipal bonds where the securities were not in default.
In its statement, Peacock, Hislop, Staley & Given stressed that the SEC has not alleged that any investor was harmed.
The firm said the bonds have paid timely principal and interest to investors in accordance with the representations contained in the official statements.
